newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-CLARKE SHOULDERS BLAME FOR BLOWING BIG LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CLARKE SHOULDERS BLAME FOR BLOWING BIG LEAD.

text.p: Darren Clarke surrendered a four-stroke lead over the final nine holes in the third round of the British Open on Saturday and admitted he had only himself to blame.
"I made a few mistakes. I made a few bad club selections as well as a few bad swings," the Northern Irishman said.
Beginning the day nine under par, Clarke stormed to 13 under by the turn and looked to have taken a stranglehold on the tournament with Swede Jesper Parnevik his nearest challenger four strokes back.
But then the back nine holes, which have caused grief to many of the world's top golfers this week, witnessed a dramatic transformation with a six-stroke swing between the two.
Clarke, who had not dropped a stroke since the 10th hole of the second round, had bogeys at four of the last eight while Parnevik had three birdies and dropped only one shot.
The result left Clarke on a nine under par 204 going into Sunday's final round, two shots adrift of the Swede.
But afterwards Clarke, who had started the tournament as a 66-1 outsider with the bookmakers, was remarkably sanguine about the situation.
"I have a chance to win the Open tomorrow, and hopefully, if a chance does present itself for me to win, I will take it. I'm playing in the last group, it's more experience for me," he said.
"I threw away a few shots but also saved a few shots. So hopefully tomorrow I'll play those nine holes a lot better than I did today."
It is new territory for the cheerful Ulsterman who turned professional in 1990 and has just two European Tour wins behind him, the Belgian Open in 1993 and the German Masters last year.

He blamed himself for not listening to his caddie over the choice of clubs at several holes and said he would be listening to him a lot more on Sunday. "He seemed to be getting it all right a lot more than I did," he said.
Clarke said he did not see world number one Tiger Woods winning the tournament despite his record equalling 64 on Saturday.
"Jesper is eight clear of him, I'm six clear of him. I think a lot of people would have to play not so well."
